business_problem: Leapmotor wanted to turn its upgraded smart cockpit into a more natural AI interaction surface, but traditional fixed Q&A could not support open conversation, vehicle-how-to guidance, image generation, or broad knowledge queries. The automaker needed an architecture that could combine large-model dialogue, enterprise vehicle knowledge, internet knowledge, and visual generation inside one in-car assistant.
solution_summary: Leapmotor used Alibaba Cloud Bailian as the application layer for a large-model cockpit assistant rather than bolting one feature onto its existing voice stack. Qwen models power open-ended multi-turn voice interaction so drivers can move beyond fixed command trees into natural chat, general knowledge questions, and richer help flows. The assistant retrieves from both Leapmotor's own vehicle knowledge base and a broader internet knowledge base, which lets the same interaction surface answer product-specific questions, explain vehicle functions, and support route-planning or media requests with more context. For visual features, the voice assistant can call Wanxiang through the cloud model layer to generate wallpapers from speech in seconds. Bailian's unified model foundation also gives Leapmotor an extensible application architecture, so new cockpit scenarios can be added and iterated without rebuilding the serving stack each time.

solution_components.name: Bailian
solution_components.role: Provides the large-model application platform that connects dialogue, retrieval, and generation functions inside the cockpit.

solution_components.name: Qwen models
solution_components.role: Handle open-ended voice dialogue, general knowledge Q&A, and vehicle-assistance reasoning in the cockpit.

solution_components.name: Wanxiang
solution_components.role: Generates wallpapers from voice prompts as part of the entertainment experience in the vehicle cockpit.

solution_components.name: enterprise knowledge base
solution_components.role: Stores Leapmotor vehicle and feature knowledge that the cockpit assistant can retrieve during user interactions.

solution_components.name: internet knowledge base
solution_components.role: Adds broader open-domain information to the same retrieval layer for richer in-car answers.

data_flow: Voice requests enter the Bailian application layer, where Qwen models handle dialogue and retrieve context from Leapmotor's enterprise knowledge base and broader internet knowledge. For visual requests, the assistant invokes Wanxiang through the same cloud stack and returns generated cockpit wallpaper back to the in-car interface.
business_outcome: Alibaba Cloud helped Leapmotor move from rigid voice commands to a more expressive AI cockpit experience. The production system now supports conversation, vehicle knowledge Q&A, route and feature guidance, and voice-driven image generation on one extensible model foundation, giving the automaker a faster path to add new in-car AI experiences while lowering the cost and complexity of expanding cockpit use cases.
architecture_clues: A single Bailian foundation is reused across voice chat, retrieval, and image-generation scenarios in the cockpit.
The assistant combines enterprise and internet knowledge retrieval rather than relying only on one source.
Voice-driven image generation is treated as part of the production cockpit flow, not a disconnected demo feature.
The architecture is designed so new cockpit scenarios can be added on the same large-model base.
